_source:
A real 'History Form 2 Scheme of Work' (a real Zambian secondary school's Social Science Department; the source's own teacher name and school name are not reproduced here per this app's standing sourcing policy) was shared with this project via Drive, across separate Term 1 and Term 2 documents. This is a genuine gap fill -- this app previously had no History Form 2 content at all. Cites the real official '2024 History Syllabus, Ordinary Secondary Education Form 1-4' with real page citations (Term 1: pp.18-24; Term 2: pp.30-33). Term 2's own opening 3 weeks ('REVISION OF TERM 1 TOPICS') and closing 3 weeks ('REVISION OF ALL FORM 2 TOPICS') are excluded, since they name no new specific competences of their own -- only its 4 real new topics (weeks 4-6, 8) are included here.

TERM 3 REBUILT (2026-09-08) from the real, official Curriculum Development Centre 'History Teaching Module, Form 2 Term 3' (a genuine CDC publication, added to the CDC Digital Library 06/09/2026 -- no individual/school name to strip). This CORRECTS an earlier placement: this file previously carried these same two topics (2.5 Resistance to Colonial Rule, 2.6 Zambia's Struggle for Independence) under Term 1, based on the one real school's own scheme -- the official CDC Teaching Module confirms both belong in Term 3 instead, and its own real content (introductions, hooks, key words, full learning activities) is markedly richer than the school scheme's brief one-line competency entries, so it now supersedes that placement. A real irregularity in the official module itself is documented, not silently corrected: its own Sub-topic 2.5.1 and Specific Competence code are both printed as '2.3.1'/'2.3.1.1' (a copy-paste artifact from an earlier template) even though the topic itself is unambiguously 2.5, referenced consistently everywhere else in the module (table of contents, running headers, its own introduction) -- this file uses the topic-consistent '2.5.1' numbering instead of reproducing the source's own typo.

Same-day cross-check: the real, official CDC 'History Form 2 Terms 1 and 2' Teaching Module (on the CDC Digital Library since 27/04/2026) was also checked and confirms this file's own Term 1 content (2.1 Slavery and Slave Trade through 2.4 Colonial Administration, including sub-topic 2.1.4 Slave Trade and Black Friday) matches the real official module exactly -- no changes needed there. That same official module explicitly states it covers 'form 2 level, particularly term 1 and term 2' but its own table of contents lists no topic beyond 2.4 -- this file's own Term 2 content (3.1 Copper Mining through 3.4 The Pan-African Movement) is NOT covered by either official Teaching Module checked, but is left exactly as originally sourced since it carries its own real official syllabus page citations (pp.30-33) from a different real document -- Teaching Modules are known to not always cover every real syllabus topic in full lesson-plan depth, so an absence from a Teaching Module's own table of contents is not by itself evidence the syllabus topic isn't real.

Its own Content/Concept, Learning Activities, Strategies/Methods and Materials/Resources columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for every other bundled subject in this app.

subject.name: History
subject.description: Ordinary Level Secondary History syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre, 2024).

grade.name: Form 2
grade.phase: Secondary — the source syllabus itself uses "Form 1-4" for Ordinary Level Secondary under the 2023 CBC, not "Grade".

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1 Development of Slavery and Slave Trade
sub_topics.description: Meaning of slavery and slave trade; forms; reasons; impact; abolition.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.2 Europe and the Benefits from Slave Trade

competencies.description: Analyse Europeans' benefits from slave trade

sub_topics.description: Benefits European countries gained from the slave trade (infrastructural development, corporations).

sub_topics.name: 2.1.3 Human Trafficking as a Modern Form of Slave Trade
sub_topics.description: Human trafficking; its forms and effects; demonstrating respect for rights.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.4 Slave Trade and Black Friday

competencies.description: Relate Black Friday to modern day commerce

sub_topics.description: Origin of the term 'Black Friday'; its adoption in Zambia.

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1 Missionary Work in Zambia

competencies.description: Analyse impact of missionary activities in Zambia

sub_topics.description: Missionary groups in Zambia; their aims, activities, and impact (education, health, colonialism).

topics.name: 2.3 Establishment of Colonial Rule in Zambia

sub_topics.name: 2.3.1 British Occupation of Northern Rhodesia

competencies.description: Analyse process of colonial occupation of Northern Rhodesia

sub_topics.description: Motives for colonisation; formation of Northern Rhodesia; process of occupation.

sub_topics.name: 2.4.1 Types of Governance in Northern Rhodesia
sub_topics.description: Types of colonial governance (direct/indirect rule); features; impact; neo-colonialism.

sub_topics.name: 2.4.2 The Central African Federation (1953-1963)

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of Central African Federation

sub_topics.description: Formation of the Federation; African collaboration to dismantle it; current collaboration.

sub_topics.name: 3.1.1 The History of Copper Mining in Zambia
sub_topics.description: Background of copper mining in Zambia (pre-colonial to post-colonial); its impact (economic, social, political).

sub_topics.name: 3.2.1 Labour Migration in Colonial and Post-Colonial Zambia

competencies.description: Assess impact of labour migration in colonial and post-colonial Zambia

sub_topics.description: Causes of labour migration; recruiting organisations (e.g. WENELA); impact of labour migration.

sub_topics.name: 3.3.1 Zambia's Role in the Liberation Struggle of Southern Africa

competencies.description: Evaluate Zambia's role in the liberation struggle of Southern Africa

sub_topics.description: Countries Zambia helped to liberate; Zambia's role (hosting leaders, diplomacy, support); impact on Zambia.

sub_topics.name: 3.4.1 The Pan-Africanism

competencies.description: Promote unity in Africa through Pan-Africanism

sub_topics.description: Aims of the Pan-African movement; role of African leaders (Kaunda, Nkrumah); efforts to achieve it.

topics.name: 2.5 Resistance to Colonial Rule in Northern Rhodesia
topics.description: In the late 19th century, European powers scrambled to colonise Africa and Northern Rhodesia was no exception. The British South Africa Company, led by Cecil Rhodes, expanded its influence in the region, leading to its colonisation; Northern Rhodesia remained under British control for almost 70 years. In the 1940s a wave of awakening became known as resistance to colonial rule -- this topic covers the different forms colonised people used to push back against foreign control, primary and secondary.

sub_topics.name: 2.5.1 Primary and Secondary Resistance to Colonial Rule

competencies.description: Interpret resistance methods to colonial rule

sub_topics.description: Resistance to colonial rule changed character over time. Primary/early resistance was organised by individual communities and traditional leaders, often direct opposition to colonial authority. Secondary/later resistance was more organised and involved wider sections of the population -- welfare associations, religious movements, trade unions, political organisations, strikes, boycotts, petitions and demonstrations.

topics.name: 2.6 Zambia's Struggle for Independence
topics.description: Zambia officially gained independence on 24 October 1964, transforming from the British protectorate of Northern Rhodesia into a sovereign Republic. This independence was achieved through many sacrifices made by people who risked their lives for their nation's freedom -- this topic covers the nationalists in Zambia's independence struggle.

sub_topics.name: 2.6.1 Nationalists in Zambia's Independence Struggle

competencies.description: Appreciate the role of nationalists and Freedom fighters during Independence struggle

sub_topics.description: The role of Zambia's leading nationalists in the struggle for independence (e.g. Dauti Yamba, Godwin Mbikusita Lewanika, Harry Mwaanga Nkumbula, Kenneth Kaunda, Simon Mwansa Kapwepwe, Mainza Chona, Julia Mulenga Nsofwa) and other individuals in the resistance struggle; demonstrating respect to Zambia's nationalists and freedom fighters.
